edition.window: Orders and decisions passed or reported between 10:00 AM IST on 23 November 2026 and 10:00 AM IST on 24 November 2026

items.caseName: Jay Ambe Petrochem and Infra v. Techno Global Services Private Limited
items.coram: Bidisha Banerjee (Judicial Member) and Rekha Kantilal Shah (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Kolkata: An expected default is not enough to issue an IBC demand notice
items.text: The Kolkata bench dismissed an operational creditor's Section 9 petition because the Section 8 demand notice went out before the 30-day contractual credit period on the March 2023 invoices had run out. It also found a genuine pre-existing dispute over about Rs 83.45 lakh that the debtor said it paid directly to vendors. Calling the petition a pressure tactic and an abuse of process, the bench imposed Rs 1 lakh in costs.

items.caseName: Sakhy Thomas v. M/s Nucleus Premium Properties Pvt Ltd and Ors
items.coram: Vinay Goel (Judicial Member) and Ravichandran Ramasamy (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Kochi: Successful resolution applicant cannot use the approved plan to forcibly evict a flat allottee
items.text: The tribunal held that Buildwell, the successful resolution applicant for Nucleus Premium Properties, could not take possession of a flat by force on the strength of the approved resolution plan, since about Rs 44.61 lakh had been paid for it. It ordered possession restored to the person dispossessed, with costs running from the date of dispossession. It left the question of legal heirs to the succession proceedings pending in the Delhi High Court.

items.caseName: Central Bank of India v. Hind Industries Ltd
items.coram: Praveen Gupta (Judicial Member) and Ashish Verma (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Allahabad: Bank's insolvency plea admitted against corporate guarantor Hind Industries over Hind Agro's dues
items.text: The bench admitted Central Bank of India's Section 7 petition against Hind Industries, guarantor for credit given to Hind Agro Industries, over a default of about Rs 36.50 crore. It held that a guarantor's liability is co-extensive with the borrower's, that the balance left unpaid under Hind Agro's resolution plan stays recoverable, and that a DRT order of April 2024 restarted limitation. It began CIRP, imposed a moratorium and appointed an interim resolution professional.

items.caseName: Impresario Vs. Colorbar Cosmetics Pvt. Ltd.
items.coram: Justice Rajesh Bindal (Chairperson), Barun Mitra and Indevar Pandey (Technical Members)
items.headline: NCLAT New Delhi: Rejection of vendor's insolvency plea against Colorbar Cosmetics upheld
items.text: The appellate tribunal found no error in the NCLT Delhi order of 30 September 2026 that refused to admit Impresario's petition over about Rs 4.39 crore for goods supplied. Colorbar had alleged kickbacks and inflated procurement involving former employees and vendors, and had filed a police complaint naming Impresario. The NCLAT agreed that this was a real pre-existing dispute that barred CIRP.

items.caseName: N. Mohanraj v. Atlantic Granites Private Limited & Ors.
items.coram: Jyoti Kumar Tripathi (Judicial Member) and Ravichandran Ramasamy (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Chennai: Selling a struck-off company's property is an irregularity, not fraud in itself
items.text: The bench held that a petition about misconduct in a struck-off company can be brought under Sections 248(7) and 252 of the Companies Act. It found no prima facie case for an investigation into the 2019 sale of part of the company's land, which was alleged to be undervalued. Because the company never started business, the petition was dismissed and the sale issue was left to the Registrar of Companies.

items.caseName: Bata India Limited v. Commissioner of GST & Central Excise
items.coram: Ajayan T.V. (Judicial Member) and Vasa Seshagiri Rao (Technical Member)
items.headline: CESTAT Chennai: Rs 1.13 crore CENVAT credit demand against Bata India set aside
items.text: The tribunal held that the Revenue could not deny credit on services received at Bata's corporate office and distribution centres for the Hosur factory, because an earlier 2018 ruling on the same issue had become final. It added that exclusion clauses raised by the Commissioner (Appeals) but missing from the show cause notice could not be relied on. The demand, interest and a Rs 10 lakh penalty were all set aside.

items.caseName: Gravity Bath Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. v. Principal Commissioner of Customs (Import), ICD-TKD, New Delhi
items.coram: Dr. Rachna Gupta (Officiating President) and Hemambika R. Priya (Technical Member)
items.headline: CESTAT Delhi: Duty, confiscation and penalties upheld against Gravity Bath for undervaluing Chinese imports
items.text: The bench dismissed all seven appeals. It found that the Section 108 statements were backed by supplier invoices, WhatsApp chats and electronic records with valid Section 138C certificates, and that the late retractions carried no weight. It upheld revaluation under Rule 12, the refusal to allow cross-examination, and penalties on co-noticees who knew about the undervaluation.

items.caseName: The Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax v. Samanvay Sparsh
items.coram: Sanjay Garg and Narendra Prasad Sinha
items.headline: ITAT Ahmedabad: Only the profit element of a builder's on-money is taxable, and Section 115BBE does not apply
items.text: The tribunal dismissed the Revenue's appeals for AY 2019-20 and 2020-21 over on-money of about Rs 14.23 crore, recorded in an Excel sheet found during a survey. It upheld the CIT(A)'s 15% profit estimate and the set-off against excess stock already offered to tax. Because the receipts were tied to the construction business, it held them to be business receipts outside Section 115BBE.

items.headline: ITAT Ahmedabad: Assessment in the name of a company already merged into Schaeffler India is invalid and cannot be cured under Section 292B
items.text: LUK India had merged into Schaeffler India with effect from 1 January 2018. Even after being told of the merger, the Assessing Officer passed an assessment order dated 17 January 2020 in LUK India's name. The tribunal treated this as a substantive illegality, not a procedural slip, and held that Section 292B could not save the order.

items.headline: ITAT: Singapore firm's income from floating production solutions for oil and gas to be assessed under Section 44B
items.text: The Singapore-resident assessee challenged a final assessment of January 2025 passed after DRP directions. The dispute concerned a technical collaboration agreement with OCS Services (India) for hook-up and commissioning of the FPSO Ruby in the Krishna-Godavari basin. According to the report, the tribunal held the income taxable under Section 44B, not as fees for technical services under Section 9(1)(vii) read with Section 44D.

items.headline: ITAT Surat: Target-linked family trips for dealers are deductible business promotion expenses under Section 37(1)
items.text: During scrutiny, the Assessing Officer questioned about Rs 19.95 lakh claimed by the Surat trading firm as business promotion expenses. The tribunal held that family trips for dealers who meet sales targets are directly linked to turnover. It allowed them as business expenditure under Section 37(1).

items.headline: ITAT: PCIT cannot use Section 263 revision on a debatable view about Section 28 Land Acquisition Act interest
items.text: For AY 2019-20, the issue was whether interest under Section 28 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 on enhanced compensation is taxable as income from other sources or forms part of exempt compensation. According to the report, the tribunal held that revision under Section 263 cannot be invoked where the Assessing Officer took one of two possible views on a debatable issue.

items.headline: ITAT Chennai: Temple trust's Section 12AB registration plea restored after rejection over 'unreadable' documents
items.text: The CIT(E) had rejected the trust's Form 10AB application on 23 June 2026, on the ground that the documents filed were unreadable, invalid or corrupted. The tribunal allowed the appeal, set aside the rejection and sent the application back to the CIT(E) for fresh consideration.

items.headline: ITAT Bangalore: Agriculturist's explanation for property buys and deposits remanded despite no ITR filed
items.text: The Assessing Officer had completed a best-judgment reassessment for AY 2016-17 at about Rs 1.90 crore, treating property investments and bank deposits as unexplained, and the CIT(A) dismissed the appeal for delay. The tribunal held that the assessee's claim that the money came from agricultural income must be examined on merits. It sent the matter back to the Assessing Officer for fresh adjudication.

items.headline: GSTAT Agra: No Section 129(3) penalty for machinery sent for repair without an e-way bill when documents were valid
items.text: The taxpayer sent a defective machine from Vidisha to Faridabad for repair with the original invoice, a transport bilty and a Rule 55 delivery challan, but without an e-way bill. The tribunal treated the lapse as technical, since the department showed no intent to evade tax, and held that no penalty was leviable.

items.headline: GSTAT Agra: Unproven vehicle-breakdown claim cannot excuse e-way bill mismatch; Rs 6.38 lakh penalty restored
items.text: Goods moving from New Delhi to Firozabad were intercepted near the Tundla toll plaza in a vehicle different from the one named in the e-way bill. The breakdown explanation came months later with no proof. The tribunal held that this could not excuse the failure to update vehicle details under Rule 138(5), and restored the penalty.

items.headline: GSTAT Agra: Excess ITC in GSTR-3B over GSTR-2A alone cannot sustain a demand once the explanation is accepted
items.text: The Assessing Officer flagged ITC claimed in GSTR-3B for FY 2022-23 that exceeded what GSTR-2A showed, but the first appellate authority accepted the taxpayer's explanation. The tribunal dismissed the department's appeal, finding no error in that order.

items.headline: CESTAT Kolkata: No consignment notes, no GTA service; Rs 2.73 crore service tax demand on truck owner quashed
items.text: The department had treated about Rs 18.23 crore of gross receipts shown in the truck owner's income tax return for FY 2016-17 as taxable consideration, based on CBDT data. The tribunal held that carrying goods by road without issuing consignment notes is not a goods transport agency service. It set the demand aside.
